title: Why do most people prefer to play rather than create, even when AI makes it "easy"?
author: gkhachik
selftext:
Building this wasn't easy. My AI engineer and I spent countless nights wrestling with our DeepSeek orchestrator base before launch. But it works! The generated games are surprisingly high-quality, and we're currently adding features to let users generate games from GIFs, memes, or stickers.

But here’s the problem - despite hitting 3,000 daily users, 90% of users are just playing the games made by the other 10%.

To push people to create, I hosted a 1-month game jam with prizes for the top 3 user-generated games. I expected a massive spike, but it only bumped the daily creation rate up by 2%.

I’m frustrated but not giving up. I genuinely believe playing your own creation is a dream for many gamers.

Why most people prefer to play rather than create, even when AI makes it "easy"?

comments.author: florodude
comments.body: User generated...in what? Most people are smart enough to know they can just dev with claude and not whatever flavor of the week creation website there is

comments.author: ArtificialImages
comments.body:
Why would anyone use your ai game maker rather than just using ai themselves?

Seriously though? Even if its easier. Even if its higher quality. I still would NEVER. 

I can yknow... share and sell games i make with ai. I can't do that with yours. I dont own your ai game maker. I own the games my ai makes for me. 

Those that want to make games with ai likely dont want to use a more limited tool to do it. 

And just in general most want to play. Not make.

replies.author: gkhachik
replies.body:
The point you shared is true, but it's all about the different thing, with the in-app community and a remix feature that allows anyone to build on someone else’s game, I wouldn’t consider the tool’s potential limited or nobody wants to use it, we have 10X monthly growth and high percentage of returning users. There’s certainly room for improvement, but even users who only know how to prompt and have no interest in diving deep into game development could make it a small part of their daily routine.

The goal is to make game creation feel as simple and intuitive as playing a game itself. That’s why I believe that, for an app like mine, 30–40% of users could create at least one game.

replies.author: ArtificialImages
replies.body:
Listen. It's clear its going very well.

What is the issue? 

10% of users actually making games is massive. Like... massive.

3000 users is huge. Thats 300 creators on YOUR PLATFORM. 

I would literally do anything for that. So whats the issue?

You want more of those people creating? Maybe you're just expecting too much. Don't look a gift horse in the mouth and all that. If it works dont break it etc etc. 

I don't see the issue. Your numbers are fine. Fantastic even.

comments.author: Nessuno256
comments.body:
Easy? I’m a game developer with over 10 years of experience, and I use AI tools very actively in my work now. The technical side has indeed become much easier, but the amount of effort and time required to make a game worth playing is still enormous.

I don’t believe in “one-shot” generated games - not at this stage of development, no.

replies.author: gkhachik
replies.body:
I agree with you, and I think I may not have explained the vision clearly enough. I didn’t build this app for professionals like you, but for people who have always dreamed of making their own games but never had the technical skills to do so.

I also believe creators like you could play a huge role in helping them get started. For example, you could share your expertise with our community, organize game jams directly in the app to find people with real potential.

We were backed by Google a few months ago, and we’d love to collaborate with experienced game creators like you to give people the tools, guidance, and confidence they need to take their first steps and believe that making their own game is possible.

comments.author: Valdaraak
comments.body: Wait a minute, I've seen this video before. The [last post I saw this on](https://old.reddit.com/r/aigamedev/comments/1x1l1h7/how_i_created_an_ai_game_in_under_5_minutes_using/) said the game was made with Gemini and posted by a different user.

replies.author: gkhachik
replies.body: Nobody is lying. I never said I created the game myself. I simply chose it as a reference for the post. The creator you shared is credited as the original owner of the game in my app.

replies.author: Valdaraak
replies.body:
Just odd you would've chosen the exact same game video that was shared here a couple days ago *and* got a poor reception.

To answer the primary question you asked:

People are still playing rather than creating because creating something *good* still isn't easy and people are lazy.

replies.author: gkhachik
replies.body: Thanks for the feedback! You're absolutely right. I hadn't noticed this.

comments.author: gkhachik
comments.body: For anyone who’d like to try the app and get a better sense of what I’m talking about, you can check it out here: [https://klipy.com/open](https://klipy.com/open)

comments.author: Master-Ideal3826
comments.body: Free AI game makers are hard to find, basically.
